newsitem.title: INDIA: India shares end down as speculative interest dips.
newsitem.headline: India shares end down as speculative interest dips.

text.p: ** - Stocks across Indian bourses close lower as
speculators unwind long positions in index stocks
** Bombay's benchmark index loses 58.25 pts, or 1.72 pct to
3,324.22, off 3,381.72 after Friday's 3.6 pct fall
** Lack of follow-up government measures after repeated
promises of policy package dampens market sentiments
** Bank stock SBI takes a severe beating in hectic trade
** National Stock Exchange 50-stock index falls 25.0 pts,
2.57 pct to provisional 946.40 in extended trade
** Calcutta index sheds 1.20 pct to 435.37 and Madras index
down 1.84 pct to 3,237.46
Dissapointment over failed government promises sparked renewed selling in Indian shares on Monday with the Bombay index falling 1.7 percent, dealers said.
"Speculators are running for cover. The lack of buyers is hitting the market hard," said a dealer at a foreign brokerage.
Traders said an absence of positive news after the government last week failed to announce promised market policy initiatives weighed heavy on minds of major players.
"Everyone's disappointed and frustrated with the market. The speculators have all gone quiet," said the chief dealer at a London-based broking firm.
Share prices rose sharply in January on frequent assurances by Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda that his government would unveil a series of new market-friendly policy initiaties.
But Finance Minister P. Chidambaram dashed hopes last week when he said the expected package actually consisted of measures already taken since January.
Bombay's index reacted sharply, plunging 127.58 points, or 3.6 percent, to 3382.47 on Friday.
Analysts said they were advising investors to pick up stocks at declines. "The mood now is to only look for specific good stock ideas," said Alok Sethi, director at Natwest Securities.
At the Bombay Stock Exchange, (BSE) SBI lost 12.50 rupees, or 4.6 percent to end at 259.0 in volumes of 6.88 million shares. The Delhi index fell 2.54 percent to 713.06.
Pivotals ended with sharp losses. Share prices at the National Stock Exchange also fell.
"A lot of stock is getting liquidated...there has also been some fund-based selling," said Dilip Joshi, dealer at Prime Broking.
-- ANSHUMAN DAGA, Bombay equities desk +91-22-265 9000
